opmerking: Checked the English pages of each clinic's own site through a fetch tool that obeys robots.txt. No clinic's site says that the named surgeon personally does the key steps. Yanhee, Bangkok Hospital, Phyathai and PPSI publish prices in THB. Only PPSI publishes a written revision policy. News was searched in English and Thai. Not one named clinic in this list turned up a death, a regulator ruling or a licence problem in a trusted source; the only named case is an old Bumrungrad court ruling that has nothing to do with cosmetic surgery. Recent deaths and raids involve clinics that the reports do not name, so they are listed under algemeen. Phuket International Hospital's site now shows itself as Bangkok Hospital Siriroj, and PPSI runs inside that hospital.

algemeen.wat: CIB and the Thai FDA raided a clinic in Khlong Toei, Bangkok, that made injectable cosmetic drugs in an unlicensed, unsterile lab; officers seized 3,367 items worth more than THB 10 million, including 776 bottles of unregistered drugs. The clinic was not named.
Thai authorities opened an investigation after a 43-year-old British man died following a penis enlargement procedure at a Bangkok clinic. The reports do not name the clinic.

The CIB and Samut Sakhon public health office arrested five people for practising medicine or dentistry without a licence at five sites, one of them an unnamed beauty clinic in Samut Prakan that gave IV drips with no doctor present.

Consumer Protection Police and the Department of Health Service Support arrested two unlicensed women who gave Botox and filler in homes they had made into clinics in Bangkok and Samut Prakan; both were charged under the Hospital Act 1998.
The DHSS announced AI-based screening of health advertising, alongside a proposal to extend the medical visa.

The DHSS inspected an unnamed clinic in Pathum Wan after a 38-year-old man collapsed following nose and chin surgery; it found the clinic registered and passed the findings on for possible legal action.
The DHSS screens online plastic surgery ads by beauty agencies and influencers for false or exaggerated claims.

After a 21-year-old died following breast augmentation at an unnamed clinic, the DHSS found that the clinic lacked life-saving equipment, had altered an operating room without permission and ran unapproved ads.
